title: Finite morphisms that are locally finitely presented are finitely presented
statement: Let $p:T\to U$ be a finite morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. If $p$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], then $p$ is of finite presentation: it is quasi-compact and separated (because finite morphisms are affine and separated), and together with local finite presentation this is the definition of finite presentation.
